newsitem.title: FRANCE: Le Pen slams France over Zhirinovsky visa.
newsitem.headline: Le Pen slams France over Zhirinovsky visa.

text.p: French far-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen slammed the government on Wednesday for denying a full visa to Russian nationalist extremist Vladimir Zhirinovsky, saying it smacked of anti-Slavic racism.

Le Pen, himself under fire for saying last month that racial inequality was a "fact", said he met Zhirinovsky at Paris' Charles de Gaulle on Wednesday after the Russian attended a session of the 39-nation Council of Europe in Strasbourg.
Zhirinovsky's visa lets him visit Strasbourg, eastern France, but restricts him to airports in others part of France.
"Isn't there a whiff of anti-Slavic racism here by the French government?" Le Pen asked in a statement, saying Zhirinovsky was a leading Russian parliamentarian and democrat.

Zhirinovsky gained notoriety in France in 1994 when he hurled plants and dirt and spat back at Jewish demonstrators at the Russian consulate in Strasbourg, when he was attending a previous session of the Council of Europe.

Le Pen, who attended Zhirnovsky's silver wedding celebraytion in Moscow in February, said it was astonishing the Russian was barred while "any illegal immigrant, drug trafficker, crook, vandal or other paedophile can get in amid general indifference."
